caribbean.name: Caribbean
caribbean.remarks: Not a country and not quite a sea — the islands, the water between them, and the reef that ties the two together. Where a great many divers learn, and where a great many go back.

greater_antilles.name: Greater Antilles
greater_antilles.remarks: The four large islands at the northern edge of the Caribbean, sitting on their own tectonic plate.

lesser_antilles.name: Lesser Antilles
lesser_antilles.remarks: A volcanic arc curving south from Puerto Rico, marking where one plate is sliding beneath another.

gulf_of_mexico.name: Gulf of Mexico
gulf_of_mexico.remarks: Nearly enclosed, and the Loop Current spins through it before leaving as the Gulf Stream. There is an asteroid crater under its southern edge with a good deal to answer for.

gulf_of_california.name: Gulf of California
gulf_of_california.remarks: Long, narrow and startlingly productive — Cousteau called it the world's aquarium, and the description has stuck to it ever since.

hudson_bay.name: Hudson Bay
hudson_bay.remarks: Frozen much of the year, and shallow enough that it is really a flooded dent in the continent.

beaufort_sea.name: Beaufort Sea
beaufort_sea.remarks: Arctic water and sea ice, north of a coast where almost nobody lives.

labrador_sea.name: Labrador Sea
labrador_sea.remarks: Where icebergs calved off Greenland drift south, and where a good deal of the Atlantic's deep water is manufactured every winter.

canada.name: Canada
canada.remarks: The longest coastline of any country by a very wide margin, on three oceans. Cold water diving, kelp forests off British Columbia, and shipwrecks preserved in the Great Lakes by fresh water and cold.

united_states.name: United States
united_states.remarks: Coral at one end, kelp at the other, freshwater springs in Florida that run clear at a constant temperature, and the wreck of a great many things in between.

mexico.name: Mexico
mexico.remarks: The Yucatan is limestone riddled with flooded caves, entered through sinkholes called cenotes. The water in them is fresh on top and salt underneath, with a visible shimmering layer between.

guatemala.name: Guatemala
guatemala.remarks: Two coasts, and Lake Atitlan inland sitting in a collapsed volcano at fifteen hundred metres.

belize.name: Belize
belize.remarks: The largest barrier reef in the northern hemisphere, and a near-circular sinkhole in the middle of it that formed as a dry cave during an ice age and flooded when the sea came back.

honduras.name: Honduras
honduras.remarks: The Bay Islands sit on the same reef system as Belize, and are where a large share of the Caribbean's dive instructors were certified.

el_salvador.name: El Salvador
el_salvador.remarks: The only country in Central America with no Caribbean coast, and volcanic crater lakes inland instead.

nicaragua.name: Nicaragua
nicaragua.remarks: Lake Nicaragua has bull sharks in it, which arrived up the river and stayed — freshwater sharks by habit rather than biology.

costa_rica.name: Costa Rica
costa_rica.remarks: Cocos Island lies five hundred kilometres offshore in the Pacific, and hammerheads school there in numbers that make the crossing worth it.

panama.name: Panama
panama.remarks: Two oceans eighty kilometres apart, with entirely different marine life on each side — separated for three million years by the isthmus itself.

cuba.name: Cuba
cuba.remarks: The largest Caribbean island, and its reefs are in better condition than most, largely because decades of restricted access kept the boats away.

jamaica.name: Jamaica
jamaica.remarks: Reef along the north coast, and Port Royal on the south — a town that slid into the harbour during an earthquake in 1692 and is still down there.

haiti.name: Haiti
haiti.remarks: Shares an island with its neighbour, and has the mountains on its side of it.

dominican_republic.name: Dominican Republic
dominican_republic.remarks: Humpbacks come to the Silver Bank offshore every winter to breed, in one of the densest gatherings anywhere.

puerto_rico.name: Puerto Rico
puerto_rico.remarks: The Puerto Rico Trench runs along its northern side — over eight kilometres deep, and the deepest water in the Atlantic.

bahamas.name: Bahamas
bahamas.remarks: Shallow banks with deep blue water dropping away at the edges, and blue holes punched down through the limestone — vertical caves that flooded when the sea rose.

cayman_islands.name: Cayman Islands
cayman_islands.remarks: Three small islands on top of a submarine ridge, with walls that begin in the shallows and go down further than anyone needs.

turks_and_caicos_islands.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
turks_and_caicos_islands.remarks: A wall on the north side that drops around two thousand metres, close enough to shore to reach in a short boat ride.

bermuda.name: Bermuda
bermuda.remarks: A thousand kilometres out in the Atlantic, and the northernmost coral reef in the world — kept alive by the Gulf Stream arriving warm. Also several hundred wrecks, for the same reason the reef is there.

antigua_and_barbuda.name: Antigua and Barbuda
antigua_and_barbuda.remarks: Reef, wrecks and a reputation for having a beach for every day of the year.

saint_kitts_and_nevis.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
saint_kitts_and_nevis.remarks: The smallest country in the Americas, volcanic, with a shallow channel between its two islands.

dominica.name: Dominica
dominica.remarks: Volcanic and steep. Champagne Reef is heated by a vent underneath and releases a constant stream of bubbles through the sand.

saint_lucia.name: Saint Lucia
saint_lucia.remarks: Two volcanic peaks rising straight out of the sea, with the reef continuing the slope underwater.

saint_vincent_and_the_grenadines.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
saint_vincent_and_the_grenadines.remarks: Black volcanic sand, which makes for excellent macro diving and dreadful photographs of the beach.

grenada.name: Grenada
grenada.remarks: Home to an underwater sculpture park, installed to take pressure off the natural reef and now colonised by it.

barbados.name: Barbados
barbados.remarks: Coral limestone rather than volcanic, which makes it flatter than its neighbours and a good deal older on top.

trinidad_and_tobago.name: Trinidad and Tobago
trinidad_and_tobago.remarks: Close enough to South America to have its wildlife, and the Orinoco's outflow brings nutrients that grow some very large brain coral.

bonaire.name: Bonaire
bonaire.remarks: The entire leeward coast is a marine park, and the shore dives are numbered with yellow stones by the roadside. Park, walk in, dive.

curacao.name: Curacao
curacao.remarks: Outside the hurricane belt, with a fringing reef running the length of the sheltered side.

aruba.name: Aruba
aruba.remarks: Dry, windy and flat, with a large wreck in shallow water that has become the island's principal dive.

british_virgin_islands.name: British Virgin Islands
british_virgin_islands.remarks: The wreck of a mail steamer lost in a hurricane in 1867 lies in shallow water here, and has been dived more or less continuously since.

united_states_virgin_islands.name: United States Virgin Islands
united_states_virgin_islands.remarks: Reef, wrecks and a national park that covers most of one island and the water around it.

greenland.name: Greenland
greenland.remarks: The largest island in the world, and about eighty percent ice. Diving here means icebergs, and icebergs roll without warning.
